title: Job-definition contract: name, handler, input schema (opaque per project), retry policy, timeout
description: A job definition is a module in the applying project's jobs directory (default ./jobs/, elicited at apply time) exporting the shape named on TAC-3101-jobs-background-job-definition.responsibilities[0]. The exported handler is an async function receiving the message body and returning a value or throwing; inputSchema is opaque per project (the applying project's own validation library); the retry policy is a bounded-attempt shape with a backoff mode; the handler timeout is a positive integer millisecond value (default 60000, floor 1000, ceiling bounded by the applied queue consumer wall-clock ceiling per ADR-3104). The jobs runtime registers every job at boot on the applied queue consumer and dispatches by name. This blueprint declares the backgroundJobs applied capability at runtime: the registration entry point walks the elicited jobs directory once at boot, and the applied surface exposes the resulting set through the operator-facing surface elicited on the manifest. The handler-timeout-seconds is elicited at apply time per ADR-3104 (default 60; floor 1; ceiling bounded by the applied queue's consumer wall-clock). A handler exceeding its timeout raises a retryable timeout error routed through the queue redelivery mechanism.
rationale: A one-shape job definition keeps the discipline uniform across the applying project's job modules; the applying project owns input validation without the blueprint prescribing a validation library.
